decision: Apply the named Fredrikshalds Teater building point at Teatergata 3 and distinguish the preserved baroque-theatre stage form from the Empire-influenced wooden architecture.
identityFindings: OSM node 866964389 and Wikidata Q10498766 identify Fredrikshalds Teater at Teatergata 3.
The building is both a museum and an active theatre and must not be reduced to a generic cultural-quarter point.
The term baroque theatre describes the preserved sloping stage, auditorium and scenic tradition; the external wooden building is classically Empire-influenced.
The theatre building, ball room and salons form one institutional place, while scenery storage and neighbouring venues are separate components.
chronologyFindings: Fredrikshalds Teater was completed and opened on 18 March 1838 after an earlier theatre from 1820 was lost in the 1826 town fire.
The building was designed by engineer-major Balthazar Nicolai Garben for Det dramatiske Selskab i Fredrikshald.
The building was expanded with social rooms in 1850.
Cinema adaptations were installed in 1937 and affected parts of the original internal arrangement.
Major restoration work led to renewed use from 1982, followed by exterior and interior restoration in 2014–2017.
The venue continues to host theatre, concerts, lectures, guided tours and other events.

stageAndCollection.collectionLimit: Not every stored scene element was made for the 1838 building; some scenery predates it and additional scenery from the former Arendal theatre is held in the collection.

the historic interior contains multiple levels and stairs

rejectedAlternatives.reason: Approximately 153 metres north-east of the theatre building and unsupported by a building or entrance object.
Represents a wider modern cultural district rather than the historic theatre building.
Supports the theatre collection but is a separate storage building across from the theatre.
Administrative contact or booking information does not replace Teatergata 3 as the building anchor.

representationLimits: The marker represents the theatre building, museum and active stage at Teatergata 3.
The radius is not a building, museum, collection, event, accessibility or access boundary.
The baroque-theatre designation must not be misread as a claim that the exterior is Baroque architecture.
Performances, tours and interior access follow current schedules, ticketing and preservation rules.
Historic stairs and level changes mean that not every interior component has equal accessibility.
